description: Electronics introduces how circuits work: safety, schematics, soldering, digital logic and binary, control and analog circuits, Ohm’s law and test equipment, and careers in electronics.

safety.note: Soldering irons are hot enough to burn instantly; work with eye protection, good ventilation and adult supervision.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.summary: Safety precautions for using, building and repairing electronic devices.

requirements.title: A schematic
requirements.summary: Drawing a simple schematic with correct symbols and explaining each part.

requirements.title: Soldering
requirements.summary: Soldering and desoldering, avoiding heat damage, and printed circuit boards.

requirements.title: Control, digital and analog
requirements.summary: How electronics are used for control, digital logic and binary numbers, and one circuit project.

requirements.summary: Ohm’s law, test equipment, resistor color codes and how circuits are assembled.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Careers in electronics and researching one of them.
